one_month_reasoning: Start at the after-hours $64.85 (-5.6% on the Q3 print), not the $68.69 close. Events in the window to 2026-11-19: (1) the 2026-10-21 session and call. The print cut FY26 ad revenue to ~$2.7B from ~$3B and FCF to ~$12.0B from ~$12.5B, guided Q4 margin to 26.0% and trimmed revenue to $51.1B; the July guide-down was followed by further weakness to a 52-week low, so I tilt slightly negative for post-guidance drift (~-1.2% on the median). (2) Estimate cuts and price-target trims over the following week (the HSBC/Wells downgrades in September show the sell-side is already moving). (3) The Nielsen Gauge for September may land in the window; the July data showed YouTube at a record 14.2%, so another Netflix share dip is the likelier read, but its price impact is small. (4) Paramount-WBD is no longer a window event: the judge approved the states' settlement on 2026-09-30 and the deal was reported closed on 2026-10-06, so it is already in the price. The NFL Thanksgiving-Eve and Christmas games fall after the window. Spread: 37%/3.5 = 10.6% monthly vol, with slightly fatter tails. Median ~$64.1. Round 2: unchanged; nothing in the supervisor's findings concerns the next month.

fair_value.method: Engine blend of a GAAP P/E leg (18x engine NTM EPS at the horizon of ~$4.19 = $75.19, weight 0.8) and a regional driver DCF to FY2030 (WACC 9.6%, g 3%: $64.44, weight 0.2 per the 17.1x forward-P/E band), less a $0.20 M&A adjustment = $73.04 per share at 2027-10-20.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 18.0x x engine NTM EPS at horizon ~$4.19 (FY27 $3.77, FY28 ~$4.40: revenue $56.2B/$61.1B, EBIT margin 33.0%/34.2%, tax 15.5%, shares -3.5% a year). Reconciled 8-peer median NTM P/E 22.45x, range 11.1-35.4x.

inputs_detail.derivation: Memberships x ARM. UCAN: the March-2026 US price rise ($7.99->$8.99 ads, $17.99->$19.99 standard) laps in March 2027; Netflix share of US TV time fell from 8.3% to 7.8-7.9% (Nielsen) while YouTube hit 14.2%; Wells Fargo estimates per-member viewing -8% vs 2023; 39% of US consumers cancelled a service in six months (Ipsos). So UCAN members ~+2-3% and ARM ~+5-6%. EMEA/LATAM/APAC helped by the 15-country ad launch from March 2027. Total 56,247 vs consensus $56.96B (+11.2%): 1.3% below, because of the engagement and CPM evidence. Round 2: the CFO said on the Q3 call 'We look to sustain double-digit revenue growth' with no FY2027 guide until January; +10.1% sits at the low end of that.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Consensus $56.96B (+11.2%) if engagement stabilises; that would add about $0.10 of EPS and ~$2/share at 19x.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 = guidance 31.5% (vs 29.5% FY2025 = F10/F3), which includes ~30bp of headcount-reduction cost (Q3 letter). FY2027 +1.5pt: the 0.3pt charge does not recur, unquantified layoff savings ('not going to specifically quantify the expense impact in 2027', CFO) and 'steadily growing margin each year' (CFO), less pressure from the ad shortfall, falling upfront CPMs (Media Dynamics) and live-sports costs. Then ~1pt a year to 36% in FY2030, a mature level capped by content-cost inflation from a merged Paramount-WBD. Disney's 12.9% streaming margin shows Netflix's scale lead. Consensus FY27 EPS $3.80 implies ~33%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 37.5% by FY2030 (the high end of round-1 views) the DCF gains ~$3 and the P/E leg ~$2.

inputs_detail.derivation: Buybacks of ~$12.5B at ~$70 retire ~178.6M shares (12,500/70; 4.26% of 4,195), less ~0.7% dilution from SBC and options (TTM SBC 487 = F46): net ~-3.5%. 4,195 x 0.965 = 4,048, rounded to 4,050. Q3 alone retired 63.9M (1.5% of the count in one quarter). I keep -3.5% over the supervisor's -3.0% because the start price ($64.85) is below my ~$70 assumption.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At -3.0% the horizon value falls ~$0.4.

inputs_detail.value: 18.0x NTM GAAP EPS (engine NTM EPS at horizon ~$4.19)
inputs_detail.derivation: Reconciled 8-peer median 22.45x: sorted 11.1 (FOXA), 15.2 (DIS), 18.5 (WMG), 22.2 (META), 22.7 (GOOGL: 340.27 / FY2027 EPS 14.97), 28.2 (AMZN), 30.4 (SPOT: 526.12 / 17.28), 35.4 (TKO); median (22.2 + 22.7) / 2 = 22.45. Round 1's 28.2x included ROKU, TTWO, LYV and CMCSA and dropped GOOGL; ROKU is now priced off Fox's $160 takeover offer, TTWO and LYV have one-off earnings bases and CMCSA is linear cable. NFLX trades at 17.1x FY27 ($64.85/$3.80). 18x is ~20% below the median: NFLX FY28/FY27 consensus EPS growth is +19% vs +23.5-33% for META/AMZN/SPOT, and the industry data show engagement-share loss (Nielsen 8.3% -> 7.8-7.9%; per-member hours -8% vs 2023) with two new scale rivals forming (Paramount-WBD closed; Fox-Roku pending). Engine P/E leg $75.19; EPS = (75.19 + 0.20 adjustment) / 18 = ~$4.19. Gate correction (2026-10-21, mixed basis): the 8-peer median mixed the run table's NTM fiscal-year blends with GOOGL and SPOT on calendar FY2027 alone. On one basis (peers.md NTM fiscal-year blend of Nasdaq.com/Zacks consensus EPS, Zacks basis for every name) the median is 20.4x: FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 -> (18.5 + 22.2) / 2 = 20.35. GOOGL is dropped (its Zacks FY2026 EPS 20.55 includes non-operating stake gains); SPOT is out of the run table (EUR reporter) and on the same blend is 526.08 / (0.504 x 13.71 + 0.496 x 17.28 = 15.48) = 34.0x, which would make a 7-name median of 22.2x. The 18x multiple itself is unchanged (judgment).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Engine: 19x gives a P/E leg of $79.38 and fair value $76.39; 17x gives $71.00 and $69.69 (about +/-$4.2 on the leg, +/-$3.35 on fair value per turn).

inputs_detail.derivation: Netflix bid for Warner Bros Discovery before Paramount won in Feb 2026, so a large acquisition is a live possibility. A full-price deal is assumed to destroy ~$4B; 20% probability in the horizon. -800 / 4,050 = -$0.20.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Supervisor uses 25%: -$0.05 more.

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis (2026-10-19) and Nasdaq/Zacks (rechecked 2026-10-20 evening: unchanged, still pre-print). My FY27 EPS: 56,246 x 33.0% = 18,561 EBIT, less ~355 net interest (7,100 x 5%) = 18,206, x 0.845 = 15,384, / ~4,084 average shares (4,195 x 0.965^0.75) = $3.77, 0.8% below consensus. FY28: 61,084 x 34.2% = 20,891 - 355 = 20,536 x 0.845 = 17,353 / 3,941 = $4.40, 2.6% below. Sources by figure: revenue $56.96B and EPS $3.80 = StockAnalysis 'Revenue/EPS Next Year' (source 19); EPS 3.80 with 15 estimates, FY2028 4.52 and FY2029 5.11 = Nasdaq.com/Zacks earnings-forecast feed (source 20; re-opened 2026-10-21). Zacks/StockAnalysis consensus: basis estimate. [gate 2026-10-21]

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Regional segment build FY26-30 (revenue $51.1B -> $69.3B), EBIT margin 31.5% -> 36%, tax 15.5%, capex 1.6%, D&A 0.8%, content cash gap 35% of incremental revenue, WACC 9.6% (beta 1.05), Gordon g 3.0%, net debt $7.1B, 4,050M shares at the horizon.

inputs_detail.derivation: Calibrated to the FY2026 revenue guide of $51.1B (+13%). Regional split follows Q3'26 reported growth (UCAN +11%, EMEA +11%, LATAM +17%, APAC +12%) with EMEA/APAC FX and Q4 live slate; 19,957x1.115+14,515x1.135+5,358x1.17+5,354x1.14 = 51,100. Derived split (estimate), not guidance: the Q3 letter guides only the total ($51.1B, +13%) and gives no regional FY2026 guidance. [gate 2026-10-21]

Fade toward the 3% terminal, now with FY2030 as a steady-state step (supervisor: the FY2029 +7.2% to 3% jump was too big). US CTV ad growth cools (eMarketer); ads rise from ~$2.7B (2026) toward ~$6B by 2030, below Omdia's $8B because 2026 came in at $2.7B vs the $3B target. Totals: 56,246 x 1.086 = 61,084; x 1.0737 = 65,588; x 1.056 = 69,263. Consensus FY28 EPS +19% (4.52/3.80) implies revenue near +10% in 2028; I sit below it.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Revenue at consensus pace (~10%) in 2028 would lift the horizon value ~$3.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 effective 1,741.4/12,722.6 = 13.7%; Q2'26 667.2/4,068.6 = 16.4%; midpoint 15.05%. Plus a ~0.45pt judgment allowance for the rising global minimum tax (Pillar Two), stated separately because it is not derived from the inputs: 15.05% + 0.45pt = 15.5%. [gate 2026-10-21: midpoint corrected from ~15.5% to 15.05%; allowance labelled judgment]
PP&E D&A only; content amortization sits inside EBIT. FY2025 333.4/45,183 = 0.74%; TTM 372.4/48,370.8 = 0.77%.

FY2025 content additions 17,096.6 less amortization 16,422.2 = 674 (Q4'25 letter). 2026 targets ~1.1x cash/amortization, with amortization up ~10% to ~18.1B, so the gap is ~1.8B on 5,917 of incremental revenue = 0.31. Q3'26 ran 1.22x (5.16B vs 4.24B). FY2027: amortization +9% to ~19.7B at 1.1x gives a gap of ~1.97B on 5,147 = 0.38. Average about 0.35.
inputs_detail.variant_view: A 1.05x ratio would roughly halve the drag, adding ~$1.5/share to the DCF.

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-yr UST 5.12% (Treasury curve, 2026-10-20) + beta 1.05 x ERP 4.5% = cost of equity 9.85%. Beta from my own weekly-return regressions of NFLX on SPY (Yahoo, to 2026-10-20): 0.92 (2y), 1.04 (3y), 1.41 (5y, dominated by the 2022 collapse), 1.10 (5y ex-2022); 1.05 sits between the 3y and ex-2022 figures. Debt: gross $15.3B (Q3 letter) at ~5% pre-tax, 4.2% after tax, 5.3% of capital vs ~$272B equity ($64.85 x 4,195M). WACC = 0.947 x 9.85% + 0.053 x 4.2% = 9.55%, rounded to 9.6%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Beta 0.92 (2y) gives a ~9.0% WACC: engine DCF $71.17, fair value $74.39 (+$1.35); beta 1.41 (5y) gives ~11.1%: DCF $51.98, fair value $70.55 (-$2.49).

inputs_detail.derivation: Nominal long-run growth below the 5.1% 10-yr yield; FY2030 growth of 5.6% steps down to it. Kept at 3% rather than higher because of the long-dated engagement and content-cost risks (YouTube, short-form video, the now-merged Paramount-WBD).
inputs_detail.variant_view: 4% closes the gap to the P/E leg (DCF $74.94).

inputs_detail.derivation: Held flat: next-12-month FCF of ~$12-13B (FY2026 guide ~$12.0B, cut from $12.5B for the timing of a real-estate transaction; TTM FCF 11,152 = F99) is assumed returned through buybacks (TTM 9,921 = F67; Q3 alone $4.8B for 63.9M shares; $22.3B authorisation left), with gross debt held near $15.3B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Supervisor uses $7.5B; the $0.4B difference is under $0.1/share.

bear.story: YouTube and short-form keep taking TV time (Netflix US share toward 7%), the 2026 price rises start to show in churn, CTV CPMs keep falling as Amazon, YouTube and a Fox-Roku combination add inventory, and the now-closed Paramount-WBD (HBO Max + Paramount+) bids up content and sports: revenue growth ~7%, margin stuck near 31-32%, P/E 14x.

base.story: Growth decelerates to ~10% in 2027 (CFO: 'sustain double-digit revenue growth'; I sit at the low end, ~1.3% below consensus revenue) as engagement softness offsets pricing and ads (~$3.8B in 2027); margin +1.5pt in 2027 then ~1pt a year to 36% in 2030; the market keeps a derated 18x NTM P/E.

bull.story: The 15-country ad expansion and live events lift ad revenue toward ~$4.5B in 2027 and the Omdia ~$8B path by 2030 (WARC: ~9.2% of global CTV ad spend in 2027); pricing sticks with churn improving; margins reach ~35% in 2028; multiple re-rates to ~22x, the peer median.

comps_summary.peer_range: Reconciled 8-peer NTM P/E 11.1x (FOXA) to 35.4x (TKO), median 22.45x (META 22.2 / GOOGL 22.7 on FY27 EPS). ROKU 45.5x, TTWO 34.1x, LYV 119.1x and CMCSA 6.3x are listed but excluded (takeover-priced, one-off earnings bases, linear cable). Forward EV/EBITDA is not available on one basis; trailing EV/EBITDA for the core names with data: DIS 9.8, TKO 11.6, META 16.2, AMZN 16.8, median 13.9x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18.0x NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon: ~20% below the 22.45x median, between WMG 18.5x and DIS 15.2x, and just above where NFLX trades now (17.1x FY27, ~18.2x NTM).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount persists through the horizon because (1) NFLX's FY28/FY27 consensus EPS growth (+19%) is below META/AMZN/SPOT (+23.5% to +33%), so on growth-adjusted terms 18x is about in line; (2) my lane's data show structural share loss: Netflix's US TV-time share fell to 7.8-7.9% from 8.3% while YouTube reached a record 14.2% (Nielsen), per-member hours are ~8% below 2023 (Wells Fargo), streaming CPMs fell ~5-6% in the 2026 upfront; (3) two scale rivals are forming: Paramount-WBD closed in October 2026 (HBO Max + Paramount+) and Fox is buying Roku (close 1H 2027). A premium over DIS/FOXA persists because NFLX's 31.5% margin is far above Disney's 12.9% streaming margin, with no linear-TV run-off and low leverage (net debt $7.1B vs ~$16B 2026 EBIT).

thesis_break_reason: $46 is ~29% below the $64.85 start and 12.1x FY27 consensus EPS ($3.80), about 8% under my bear value ($49.9) and beyond a one-sigma move (~35% vol). Trading there would mean the market prices revenue growth sliding to mid-single digits and margin expansion ending: pricing power broken (churn after the 2026 price rises, US TV share toward 7%) or content costs bid up by the merged Paramount-WBD, not ordinary volatility. Round 1 had $45; moved up with the slightly higher bear value.

key_uncertainties: Whether the fall in Netflix's share of TV time (8.3% -> 7.8-7.9%) and per-member viewing (-8% vs 2023) turns into churn and weaker pricing power, or stays a mix shift that ARM gains offset.
Ad monetisation: the 2026 ad guide was cut by ~$300M while the ad tier reaches 250M viewers and upfront commitments nearly doubled; CPMs are falling industry-wide (-5%).
Content and sports cost inflation now that Paramount-WBD has closed (HBO Max + Paramount+), Fox-Roku is pending, and NFL/sports rights reset.
Margin trajectory: no FY27 guide yet; Q4'26 26% includes restructuring; consensus implies ~33% in FY27.
Reduced disclosure (no subscriber counts; engagement report once a year from Jan 2027) keeps the multiple under pressure.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine finds that the 18x P/E leg ($75.19) implies an 8.7% WACC on my explicit drivers and 3% terminal growth; equivalently, at my 9.6% WACC it needs ~4% perpetual growth after FY2030 (engine DCF $74.94 at g = 4%) with a 36% margin held. That is plausible only if Netflix keeps penetrating international broadband homes and ads reach high-single-digit share of revenue. The long-dated risks (YouTube share gains, two consolidating rivals, CPM deflation, M&A; probability-weighted ~-$8.5/share, upside ads +$3) argue against more, which is why I stay at 18x rather than the 22.45x peer median.

sbc_treatment.note: Netflix reports only GAAP EPS and operating income, which are after SBC (~0.8-1.0% of revenue). The model uses GAAP EBIT, P/E on GAAP EPS, and shares falling 3.5% a year net of SBC dilution, so SBC is counted once. Peer NTM EPS from Zacks is on each company's consensus basis, mostly adjusted for META/AMZN/GOOGL (close to GAAP), so the peer median slightly flatters peers; one more reason to sit below it.

reasoning: Round 2. Q3 print (letter, re-read): revenue $12.87B +12%, op margin 34.6%, EPS $0.87; FY26 revenue $51.1B, ads ~$2.7B (from ~$3B), FCF ~$12.0B (from $12.5B, real-estate timing); Q4 margin 26% incl. ~120bp of layoff cost; gross debt $15.3B, net debt $7.1B; no FY27 guide, but the CFO said 'We look to sustain double-digit revenue growth' and 'steadily growing margin each year'. Start price $64.85 (after hours; Nasdaq $64.89). Supervisor findings acted on: (1) WACC rebuilt from measured beta: my own weekly regressions vs SPY give 0.92 (2y), 1.04 (3y), 1.41 (5y), 1.10 ex-2022, so beta 1.05 and WACC 9.6% (I sit 0.2pt above the supervisor's 9.4% because the 3y and ex-2022 betas are above 1.0); (2) peer median rebuilt on 8 comparable names at 22.45x (checked: GOOGL 340.27/14.97, SPOT 526.12/17.28), and ROKU is now takeover-priced (Fox 8-K); (3) explicit years extended to FY2030 with growth fading to 5.6% and margin to 36%; (4) P/E cut from 19x to 18x (round 1 sat above the ~18.2x NTM the stock trades at). Industry lane updates: Paramount-WBD is no longer a pending risk (settlement approved 2026-09-30, deal reported closed 2026-10-06), so its content-bidding effect is a near-certain long-dated cost; Fox-Roku consolidates CTV distribution; WARC/Omdia see Netflix at 9.2% of CTV ad spend in 2027 and $8B ads by 2030, which I use only in the bull case. Engine: P/E $75.19 (0.8), DCF $64.44 (0.2, now 14% below), M&A -$0.20 => $73.04; scenarios $49.9/$73.0/$95.4 at 25/50/25. Ladder: scenario centres shaded halfway from value toward the $64.85 start (x0.942) because today's price beats research blends as a forecast and post-guide-cut drift is negative; within-scenario vol ~0.24 gives ~35% total vol, near the 1-year realized 35-37%. Median ~$67.4, P(>= $69) 0.475 (round 1: 0.505). Research in round 2: 7 searches/fetches plus Nasdaq consensus and Yahoo price pulls.

discount_rate.basis: 10-yr UST 5.12% (Treasury curve, 2026-10-20) + beta 1.05 x ERP 4.5% = cost of equity 9.85%. Beta from my own weekly-return regressions of NFLX on SPY (Yahoo, to 2026-10-20): 0.92 (2y), 1.04 (3y), 1.41 (5y, dominated by the 2022 collapse), 1.10 (5y ex-2022); 1.05 sits between the 3y and ex-2022 figures. Debt: gross $15.3B (Q3 letter) at ~5% pre-tax, 4.2% after tax, 5.3% of capital vs ~$272B equity ($64.85 x 4,195M). WACC = 0.947 x 9.85% + 0.053 x 4.2% = 9.55%, rounded to 9.6%.

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: Reconciled 8-peer median NTM P/E 22.45x (DIS 15.2, FOXA 11.1, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, GOOGL 22.7 on FY2027 EPS, AMZN 28.2, SPOT 30.4, TKO 35.4; range 11.1-35.4x); 18x is a ~20% discount, GAAP EPS after SBC.

adjustments.name: Probability-weighted value-destroying acquisition
adjustments.note: Equity-level. Netflix bid for Warner Bros Discovery before Paramount won it (Feb 2026); a repeat large deal at a full price is assumed to destroy ~$4B of value, with 20% probability over the horizon: -$800M, ~-$0.20/share.

segment_build.name: UCAN
segment_build.driver_note: Paid memberships x ARM. FY26 +11.5% (Q3 +11% reported; March 2026 US price rise to $8.99/$19.99/$26.99 flows through; ads). FY27 +8.5%: price rise laps in March 2027, member growth ~2-3% with US TV-time share slipping (Nielsen 8.3%->7.8-7.9%) and cancellations rising (Ipsos 39%), ARM +5-6% from price/ads. Fades to 7%/6%/4.5% (FY28-30) as the US nears saturation.

segment_build.name: EMEA
segment_build.driver_note: Memberships x ARM. FY26 +13.5% (Q3 +11% reported, +9% FX-neutral; FX tailwind). FY27 +10%: ad tier launches in nine more EMEA countries March 2027; members ~+4%, ARM ~+5-6%. Fades to 8.5%/7.5%/5.5%.

segment_build.name: LATAM
segment_build.driver_note: Memberships x ARM. FY26 +17% (Q3 +17% reported, +12% FX-neutral). FY27 +13% with price rises in inflationary markets and ads in Colombia/Peru; fades to 11%/9%/7%.

segment_build.name: APAC
segment_build.driver_note: Memberships x ARM. FY26 +14% (Q3 +12% reported, +15% FX-neutral; India view hours +24%). FY27 +13%, member-led (low ARM, New Zealand ad launch); fades to 12%/10%/8%.

bear.story: YouTube and short-form keep taking TV time (Netflix US share toward 7%), the 2026 price rises start to show in churn, CTV CPMs keep falling as Amazon, YouTube and a Fox-Roku combination add inventory, and the now-closed Paramount-WBD (HBO Max + Paramount+) bids up content and sports: revenue growth ~7%, margin stuck near 31-32%, P/E 14x.

base.story: Growth decelerates to ~10% in 2027 (CFO: 'sustain double-digit revenue growth'; I sit at the low end, ~1.3% below consensus revenue) as engagement softness offsets pricing and ads (~$3.8B in 2027); margin +1.5pt in 2027 then ~1pt a year to 36% in 2030; the market keeps a derated 18x NTM P/E.

bull.story: The 15-country ad expansion and live events lift ad revenue toward ~$4.5B in 2027 and the Omdia ~$8B path by 2030 (WARC: ~9.2% of global CTV ad spend in 2027); pricing sticks with churn improving; margins reach ~35% in 2028; multiple re-rates to ~22x, the peer median.

model_inputs.structure_note: Single reportable segment, so the segment build is regional (UCAN, EMEA, LATAM, APAC; FY2025 base from the four 2025 quarters in the Q4'25 letter, summing to $45,184M vs reported $45,183M). Each region is paid memberships x ARM; Netflix no longer discloses memberships, so the growth splits are my estimates from Q3'26 regional growth, price moves, the ad roll-out and industry engagement data. Advertising (~$2.7B in 2026, my ~$3.8B in 2027 and ~$6B by 2030) sits inside the regions. No regional margins are reported, so every region carries the company margin path. The explicit years now run to FY2030 (growth fading to 5.6%, margin 36%) before a 3% Gordon terminal. Value comes from a GAAP-EPS P/E at the horizon (weight 0.8, against a reconciled 8-peer median) and the driver DCF (weight 0.2 from the forward-P/E band: $64.85 / $3.80 = 17.1x), less a probability-weighted M&A adjustment. Content cash above amortization (the streaming FCF swing) is modelled through nwc_pct_incr_rev. No SOTP: ads and live are too small and too entangled with subscription to value separately.
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value ($73.04). The ladder is centred lower (median ~$67) because it starts from the $64.85 after-hours price and gives the research value about half weight; see reasoning.

inputs_detail.value: 18.0x NTM GAAP EPS (engine NTM EPS at horizon ~$4.19)
inputs_detail.derivation: Reconciled 8-peer median 22.45x: sorted 11.1 (FOXA), 15.2 (DIS), 18.5 (WMG), 22.2 (META), 22.7 (GOOGL: 340.27 / FY2027 EPS 14.97), 28.2 (AMZN), 30.4 (SPOT: 526.12 / 17.28), 35.4 (TKO); median (22.2 + 22.7) / 2 = 22.45. Round 1's 28.2x included ROKU, TTWO, LYV and CMCSA and dropped GOOGL; ROKU is now priced off Fox's $160 takeover offer, TTWO and LYV have one-off earnings bases and CMCSA is linear cable. NFLX trades at 17.1x FY27 ($64.85/$3.80). 18x is ~20% below the median: NFLX FY28/FY27 consensus EPS growth is +19% vs +23.5-33% for META/AMZN/SPOT, and the industry data show engagement-share loss (Nielsen 8.3% -> 7.8-7.9%; per-member hours -8% vs 2023) with two new scale rivals forming (Paramount-WBD closed; Fox-Roku pending). Engine P/E leg $75.19; EPS = (75.19 + 0.20 adjustment) / 18 = ~$4.19. Gate correction (2026-10-21, mixed basis): the 8-peer median mixed the run table's NTM fiscal-year blends with GOOGL and SPOT on calendar FY2027 alone. On one basis (peers.md NTM fiscal-year blend of Nasdaq.com/Zacks consensus EPS, Zacks basis for every name) the median is 20.4x: FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 -> (18.5 + 22.2) / 2 = 20.35. GOOGL is dropped (its Zacks FY2026 EPS 20.55 includes non-operating stake gains); SPOT is out of the run table (EUR reporter) and on the same blend is 526.08 / (0.504 x 13.71 + 0.496 x 17.28 = 15.48) = 34.0x, which would make a 7-name median of 22.2x. The 18x multiple itself is unchanged (judgment).
